51269005.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human N-terminal poly histidine-tagged PTP1B (Glu2 to Asn321 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51269005.references_previous: Zhang C-L, Liu S, Liu X-C, Gao J-M, Wang S-L. Discovery of novel inhibitors of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 proteins derived from Bim BH3 domain. Chin Chem Lett. 2017;28(7):1523–1527.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The Bim-BH3 peptide mimetics were synthesized, purified and quantified as described in our previous work.30 Direct binding affinity of the Bim-BH3 derived analogues to PTP1B was measured using the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technique as described in the Experimental section of Supporting Information. The results in Table 1 showed that compound SM-1, SM-2 and SM-6 bound to PTP1B with affinity Kd = 26.9 nmol/L, Kd = 128.0 nmol/L and Kd = 8.38 nmol/L, respectively. This indicated that these compounds might be PTP1B inhibitors. The binding affinity determined by SPR technique shows the binding ability of molecules to receptor/target, but it cannot reveal whether these molecules exhibit target inhibition activity. Thus, an enzyme-based PTP1B inhibitory activity experiment was needed to validate the PTP1B inhibitory effect.
